title: Enterprise launch readiness for RBAC v2 (enablement, docs, support, pilot accounts)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Objective
Coordinate enterprise launch readiness for RBAC v2 across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private: customer-facing enablement, internal training, support playbooks, and a defined pilot + rollout plan. This ticket is the cross-functional “last mile” tracker so pilots don’t stall on missing docs/FAQs/runbooks.

Why now
We’re seeing increased enterprise security gating on least-privilege, separation-of-duties, and auditability (especially for Dedicated + Private). Engineering is progressing on enforcement + audit logging, but we need complete enablement materials and an operational plan to avoid (a) deny spikes, (b) support confusion, and (c) “security review churn” due to inconsistent answers.

In scope
1) Enablement docs + external-facing narratives
- Publish RBAC v2 docs set: concepts, scopes (org/project/environment/cluster), permission catalog reference, built-in role templates, migration notes.
- Update Sales/SE Security FAQ with approved language for:
  - deny-by-default enforcement
  - audit log fields showing authz decisions (allow/deny + reason)
  - SSO/SAML interaction with RBAC (authn vs authz)
  - separation of duties (Security Admin vs Deployment Operator vs Billing)
  - break-glass controls and monitoring
- Create a lightweight “RBAC v2 overview for security reviewers” one-pager (PDF-style content) that Sales/SE can forward.

2) Support readiness
- Support/CS/SE playbook: triage for permission denied, common misconfigurations, how to identify missing role bindings vs missing permissions in templates vs stale cache/propagation.
- “Why was I denied?” guidance aligned with Console UX and API error semantics (debug header availability for admins, safe exposure rules).
- Define escalation path + on-call expectations during pilots (who to page for suspected regressions/bypasses).

3) Pilot + rollout coordination
- Identify 2–3 pilot accounts (mix of Dedicated + Private). Proposed initial set:
  - Ironbank Financial (Dedicated/regulated; SIEM export required)
  - Northbridge Healthcare (Private POC; strict admin separation)
  - Aegis Insurance Group (Dedicated; SSO + auditability)
- Define success criteria + instrumentation for pilots:
  - deny rate baseline vs RBAC v1 (dual-read comparison where available)
  - top denial reason codes and time-to-resolution
  - authz middleware latency impact
  - number of support tickets tagged rbac-v2
- Draft customer comms plan: what changes, what stays backward compatible, and “what to do if you see 403 permission denied.”

Out of scope
- Building new console UX beyond already committed scope (tracked elsewhere).
- ABAC/custom per-customer policy language.

Acceptance criteria
- Docs: RBAC v2 docs published and reviewed (Security + Product + Solutions Eng). Links collected in this ticket.
- Security FAQ: updated entry set approved by Security & Compliance (Aisha/MARCUS) and Sales Enablement.
- Support playbook: published with an internal training session completed; includes concrete examples (audit export denied; routing policy edit denied; key rotation denied).
- Pilot list: named accounts confirmed with owner + start date; success metrics and dashboards identified.
- Rollout checklist: single checklist covering flags, monitoring, rollback, comms, and evidence artifacts for SOC2 questionnaires.

Key stakeholders
- PM: Naomi Feldman
- PgM: Talia Benson (owner)
- Security Eng: Marcus Lin
- GRC/evidence: Olga Petrov, Daniel Carter
- Support enablement: (via Support lead; loop in as needed)
- Docs: Elliot Price, Kira Thompson
- Private pilots: Colin O’Donnell
- Audit export/SIEM: Kevin Osei

Open questions
- Which denial reason codes can be safely exposed to end-users vs only to org admins (Console + API)? Need final stance from Security.
- Default role templates for Private installs: do we ship “Private Deployment Operator” as default recommended, or keep as opt-in template?
- Feature flag naming and customer-visible behavior: how we explain dual-read/dual-write without over-sharing internals.

Links / artifacts (live)
- Confluence PRD: /product-docs/requirements/rbac-v2-prd-enterprise-controls
- Console UX spec: /product-docs/design-specs/console-role-management-ux
- Security FAQ draft: /sales-enablement/security-faq/rbac-v2-and-least-privilege-faq
- Runbook: /eng-platform/runbooks/rbac-v2-rollout-runbook
- Customer guidance (Support/CS): /policies-and-process/access-and-permissions/enterprise-rbac-customer-guidance

Risks
- Pilot customers experience unexpected denies after migration due to missing permission in role templates (high likelihood; mitigate via preflight checks + rapid template patch process).
- Support load spike from new 403s without clear guidance/UX (mitigate with playbook + deny reason codes + admin debug mode).
- Security review stalls due to inconsistent answers about break-glass and audit logs (mitigate with one-pager + FAQ approval gate).

They specifically asked for: (1) “read-only auditor” role, (2) separation of duties between deployment ops and security admin, (3) break-glass story. Please ensure one-pager includes those.

2025-02-24 (Marcus Lin): For security FAQ, we need explicit statement: deny-by-default, all sensitive actions permission-gated at gateway and service where applicable, and audit logs include authz decision fields + policy version. Also: break-glass is time-bound, requires approval, and is monitored/alerted. I’ll review final copy but please avoid promising customer-configurable ABAC.

2025-03-07 (Elliot Price): Docs PR is in progress; biggest gap is a clean “Scopes explained” section with concrete examples (org vs project vs env vs cluster). Waiting on PM-661 final scoping language to avoid rewriting. Suggest we publish docs in two phases: concepts + templates first, then deep scope examples once locked.

2025-03-11 (Kira Thompson): Drafted Support runbook outline: how to interpret 403s, checking role bindings, using admin debug header, common pitfalls (stale cache after role change), and rollback steps. Need confirmation from Eng on cache invalidation expectations so we don’t mislead Support.

2025-03-18 (Talia Benson): Pilot candidates confirmed by Sales: Ironbank (Dedicated) and Northbridge (Private). Aegis likely but timing dependent on SSO readiness. Next step: define pilot start gates—must have (a) updated FAQ, (b) support playbook v1, (c) rollout dashboard links. Assigning owners below in checklist.

2025-03-26 (Naomi Feldman): Please treat this as a release-blocker for enterprise GA messaging. We can pilot behind flags without everything perfect, but we cannot claim “enterprise-ready RBAC v2” until FAQ + support playbook + evidence-friendly audit log example are approved.
